name: EP-01 Project Foundation and Architecture
w: Stand up the Next.js 15 + TypeScript + Tailwind + Supabase skeleton, the SQL migration pipeline and the shared domain types. Every other epic needs a place to live and a repeatable way to change the database, so this comes first.
ac: Repo, app shell, UI primitives and dev tooling run locally
Supabase project wired through env vars, plus local Supabase via Docker
Repeatable SQL migration workflow that works on a fresh database
Shared domain types and a reusable Zod validation layer
out: No product features, no CI or deployment work (that is EP-09).
dod: All 10 subtasks complete. A fresh clone can be booted by following the README verbatim.

name: EP-02 Authentication and Authorization
w: Owners must be able to sign up, log in and be correctly identified, because every row in the database is scoped to an authenticated owner or staff member. Contains the identity root (profiles) that all RLS policies depend on.
ac: profiles table linked to auth.users with role and hostel scope
Owner signup, login, logout and password reset
Session-aware middleware protecting all /app routes
RLS enabled on profiles and a reusable role-guard helper
out: No social/OAuth login. No resident or tenant login accounts in the MVP. No platform-admin console.
dod: All 7 subtasks complete. An anonymous user can read no application data, proven by a direct REST call with the anon key.

name: EP-03 Hostel Onboarding and Tenant Isolation
w: An owner must be able to register a hostel and land in a working workspace, and that hostel data must be provably isolated from every other hostel. This epic carries the multi-tenant guarantee for the whole product.
ac: hostels table with ownership and identity fields
hostel_id tenant scoping with enforced RLS policies
Two-step onboarding wizard with validation and resumable drafts
Hostel settings edit page and multi-hostel switcher
Duplicate hostel prevention
out: No hostel branding, no photography uploads, no subscription or billing fields in the MVP.
dod: All 7 subtasks complete. Two separate owners cannot see or mutate each other's hostel rows, proven by test.

name: EP-04 Room and Bed Inventory Setup
w: Turn a physical hostel into structured room and bed inventory. Bed-level records are the unit that allocation, occupancy and fees all hang off, so the inventory model must be right before residents arrive.
ac: rooms and beds schema with capacity and uniqueness constraints
Room creation form, plus bulk generation for ranges like 101-110
Beds auto-generated from room capacity with stable labels
Room inventory list with filters, edit, archive and safe-delete rules
Bed status model: available, occupied, blocked, maintenance
out: No drag-and-drop floor plan editor. No per-bed pricing tiers in the MVP.
dod: All 8 subtasks complete. A 100-room hostel can be configured in under 10 minutes using bulk generation.

name: EP-05 Resident Management
w: Capture residents as first-class records with identity, contact and KYC details, so they can be allocated, billed and reported on. Duplicate prevention protects the fee ledger later.
ac: residents table with identity, contact, guardian and KYC fields
Registration form with Indian phone and age validation
Duplicate detection on normalised phone and ID proof
Searchable, filterable resident list and a full profile page
Status lifecycle: active, notice, vacated, blocked
ID proof upload to private Supabase Storage
out: No resident-facing portal or app login. No police verification or agreement document workflow.
dod: All 7 subtasks complete. Creating the same resident twice is blocked by both the UI and a database constraint.

name: EP-06 Bed Allocation and Occupancy
w: Move residents into beds and vacate them, with occupancy derived from allocations rather than guessed. This is the highest-risk area for data integrity: two residents must never hold the same bed.
ac: allocations table with start/end dates and vacate reason
Allocate a resident to a vacant bed, and vacate or transfer
Database-level guard against overlapping allocations on one bed
Occupancy counts derived from live allocations
Occupancy snapshot view per hostel and floor
Immutable allocation history and audit trail
out: No waitlist or auto-allocation engine. No bed-level housekeeping workflow.
dod: All 7 subtasks complete. A concurrency test proves two simultaneous allocations for one bed result in exactly one row.

name: EP-07 Fee and Payment Tracking
w: Let owners see who owes what and record money received. Money is tracked as invoices plus payments so partial payments and outstanding balances stay accurate and auditable.
ac: fee_structures, invoices and payments schema with integer money columns
Fee structure per sharing type with effective dates
Idempotent monthly invoice generation for occupied beds
Manual payment recording with partial payment support
Outstanding balance and due status per resident
Fee status list with paid, partial, due and overdue filters
Printable invoice and receipt view
out: No payment gateway, no UPI or card collection, no GST filing in the MVP. Recording is manual.
dod: All 7 subtasks complete. Outstanding balance for a seeded hostel reconciles exactly against invoices minus payments.

name: EP-08 Dashboard and Reporting (Basic)
w: Give the owner a single screen that answers the two questions that matter daily: how full am I, and how much money is outstanding. All values are computed from live data, never from stored counters.
ac: KPI cards: total beds, occupied, vacant, occupancy percent, collected, outstanding
Occupancy trend read model built from allocation date ranges
Recent activity and overdue-fee panels with links through to detail
Date-range filter that persists in the URL
out: No exportable PDF or Excel reports, no scheduled email digests, no per-floor analytics in the MVP.
dod: All 4 subtasks complete. Every dashboard number can be traced back to a query over allocations, invoices or payments.

name: EP-09 Security, Testing and Deployment
w: Prove the tenant isolation actually holds, protect the money and allocation rules with tests, and get the product running on a shareable staging URL. Tests here are interleaved with EP-02, EP-03, EP-06 and EP-07 rather than left to the end.
ac: Automated RLS suite proving cross-hostel access is blocked
Integration tests for allocation and fee integrity rules
GitHub Actions pipeline for lint, typecheck and tests
Staging deployment on Vercel with a separate Supabase environment
Global error boundary and safe server-side error logging
Idempotent local seed script
out: No production domain, no paid-tier monitoring, no load or penetration testing in the MVP.
dod: All 6 subtasks complete. CI is green, the RLS suite fails before policies and passes after, and the staging URL runs the full happy path.

name: EP-10 Platform Super Admin (Backlog)
w: Operator tooling for the SaaS owner: see all hostels, support a customer without asking for their password, and manage plan or suspension state. Deliberately deferred until there are real paying hostels, because building it earlier is wasted effort. No subtasks are created until this epic is scheduled.
ac: Platform-admin flag and a separate admin surface
Read-only support view into a customer hostel
Hostel suspension and plan field management
Aggregate usage metrics across hostels
out: No impersonation that can write data on behalf of a customer. No billing or invoicing to hostels.
dod: Not started. Detailed and broken into tasks only when scheduled.

name: EP-11 Notifications and Resident Communication (Backlog)
w: Automated reminders and messages: fee due reminders, payment receipts and allocation confirmations. Deferred because reminders are only trustworthy once fee data is correct, and because WhatsApp or SMS integration adds operational cost and compliance work.
ac: Fee due and overdue reminder scheduler
Payment receipt delivery to the resident
Allocation and vacate notifications to owner and resident
Delivery log with retry and failure visibility
out: No marketing campaigns or bulk SMS in this epic.
dod: Not started. Detailed and broken into tasks only when scheduled.

name: EP-12 Advanced ERP Expansion (Backlog)
w: Everything that turns a hostel manager into a full ERP: online payments, mess and attendance, complaints and maintenance, staff and payroll, visitor logs and multi-branch analytics. Explicitly backlog so the MVP can ship first.
ac: Payment gateway integration for online rent collection
Mess, attendance and meal planning modules
Complaint, maintenance and visitor management
Staff records, roles and expense tracking
Multi-branch consolidated reporting
out: Nothing in this epic is required for the MVP to be commercially usable.
dod: Not started. Detailed and broken into tasks only when scheduled.
